description_fill_in: Identifier of the source document in the 50-document corpus. Joins to corpus_manifest.csv.
Nominal file format of the source document, harmonised so each doc_id has exactly one value (the raw data listed several different formats, up to five, for the same document).
Identifier of the top-ranked text chunk returned for the query. Sequential and unique per row.
Number of words in the retrieved chunk. Values below 50 indicate a truncated chunk and are flagged as anomalies.
Similarity between the query and the top-ranked chunk; higher means a closer match. Values below 0.5 indicate retrieval failure.
Kind of question asked: factual lookup, how-to/procedure, comparison, reasoning/analysis, or request for a summary.
Quality of the generated answer (1 = fully correct and supported by the retrieved chunk, 0 = wrong or unsupported). Low values with high retrieval_score suggest hallucination.
Corpus category of the source document, looked up from corpus_manifest.csv.
The doc_type value as it appeared before harmonisation; kept for traceability.
1 if the row meets any anomaly rule (retrieval_score < 0.5, word_count < 50, or retrieval_score >= 0.85 with answer_quality_score < 0.55).
Which anomaly rule fired. Rules are checked in the order retrieval_failure, hallucination_suspect, truncated_chunk.
Binned word_count for grouping and plotting.
